requirements.evidence: Full contract present: migrations with cascading FKs, unique (queue_id, code) and the recommended index (create_tickets_table.php:15-26); Queue model fillable/casts/relations (app/Models/Queue.php:11-37); Entity::queues() (app/Models/Entity.php:36-39); enums with the required values; InactiveQueueException extends RuntimeException; IssueTicket rejects negative priority (IssueTicket.php:26-28), locks and re-reads the queue inside the transaction (:33-37) and retries on UniqueConstraintViolationException up to 5 attempts (:48-52). nextCode orders by id desc and skips codes not matching /^A(\d+)$/ with 3-digit padding that grows past 999 (Ticket.php:68-80). The write-once updating hook allows only status/called_at/called_by_user_id/updated_at (Ticket.php:25-36). call() checks membership, then re-reads under lock and rejects non-waiting tickets (Ticket.php:88-110). The factory allocates codes per insert, keeps explicit codes and has forQueue (TicketFactory.php:36-52). No requirement is missing.

conventions.evidence: The domain write goes through app/Actions/IssueTicket.php. $fillable is set deliberately through #[Fillable]. Migrations have reversible down(). PHPDoc is on the public methods. CHANGELOG.md, docs/business-rules.md and docs/database-schema.md are updated in the same change. One deviation: Ticket::call() authorizes with an inline `$user->membershipFor(...)` check (Ticket.php:90) rather than a policy/gate, while conventions.md says authorization always goes through app/Policies/. The task does dictate the method's location and exception.

security.evidence: Calling is restricted to entity members, and the ticket is left unchanged on denial (Ticket.php:90-92, tested in TicketTest.php:195-211). The inactive-queue state is read under lockForUpdate, not from the stale instance (IssueTicket.php:33-37). Priority is validated (:26-28). Immutability is enforced at the model level. No HTTP/Livewire surface, unescaped output or mass-assignment risk is introduced.

tests.evidence: IssueTicketTest covers: defaults, sequential codes with priority/channel, inactive queue with nothing persisted, a queue deactivated and a queue reactivated after it was loaded, negative priority, retry on collision and giving up after repeated collisions. TicketTest covers: enum values, queue casts/relations and per-entity slug uniqueness, factory defaults, forQueue/count/explicit code, per-queue uniqueness, every nextCode edge case from the task (A999->A1000->A1001, deleted middle ticket -> A004, A-X skipped in both scenarios, queue scoping), immutability of code/priority/channel/queue_id through save() and update(), single call, a second call, a stale instance, and non-member/no-membership callers. Only FK cascade behaviour is untested.

simplicity.evidence: The code is lean: one action, one updating hook, and a small factory store() override. No extra layers are added. Minor inefficiency: nextCode does `->orderByDesc('id')->pluck('code')` (Ticket.php:71), which loads every code of the queue into memory on each issuance just to find the first valid one.

readability.evidence: Names are clear (MUTABLE, ATTEMPTS, nextCode, forQueue), methods are small, comments are short and useful ("Re-read under lock: the in-memory status may be stale."), and the style matches Laravel stubs. There is no dead code or debug output.

scope.evidence: Every file serves the task: models, enums, exception, action, factories, migrations, the docs the task asks to update, CHANGELOG and tests. The Entity.php edit only adds the required queues() relation. There is no HTTP/Livewire/call-next code.

issues.explanation: Authorization for calling a ticket is an inline membership check instead of a policy/gate (e.g. TicketPolicy::call), which conventions.md requires for all authorization.

nextCode plucks all codes of the queue on every issuance, so issuance cost grows linearly with queue history; a lazy/cursor or chunked scan that stops at the first valid code would avoid loading everything.
The required cascade-on-delete behaviour of the entity->queues and queue->tickets FKs is not covered by a test.

review.summary: The change adds queues and tickets end to end: migrations, models, enums, exception, the IssueTicket action (row lock, DB re-check of is_active, collision retry), write-once enforcement, single call by entity members, factories, docs and CHANGELOG. Every contract item and edge case from the task is implemented and covered by meaningful tests. Only small points remain: call() authorizes inline instead of through a policy, and nextCode loads every code of the queue, so I would approve with nits.
